title: Distance Between Cities: Miles & Midpoint
description: Measure the straight-line distance between any two cities with Distance Between Cities — miles and km, initial bearing, midpoint and route. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York to Boston is approx. 190.2 miles (306.1 km) with an initial bearing of 52.3° — and their halfway point falls at 41.546, −72.551 in Connecticut.
quick_answer: Distance Between Cities measures the straight-line separation between any two cities in the world and shows more than the number: the distance in miles and kilometres, the initial bearing, the halfway point, and the curved great-circle route drawn on the map, so you can see why the shortest path bends.

Students grasp continental scale from pairs they know: the curved route to a 'nearby' European capital teaches more geography than a chapter of definitions.
Writers and researchers quoting a city separation need a reproducible figure with its method attached — this page shows its working on the map.
New York ↔ Boston: approx. 306.1 km (190.2 mi), initial bearing 52.3°, reverse 234.2°, midpoint at 41.546, −72.551. A familiar pair, and still the bearing surprises: you set off northeast, not east.

London ↔ Berlin: approx. 931.6 km (578.8 mi). On the map the great-circle route arcs gently north of the straight ruler line — the same effect, at European scale, that bends transatlantic routes toward Iceland.

faq: Which point in each city is used?

The city's published centre coordinate — the same point the search resolves to. For sprawling cities, centre-to-centre is the comparable convention; two suburbs of the same pair of cities can differ by tens of miles.
Why does the tool also show a midpoint?
Because the next question after 'how far' is usually 'where is halfway'. The midpoint is computed on the same great-circle path, ready for the Halfway Between Two Places calculator to explore.
Are the cities limited to the US and Europe?
No — the search is worldwide. This page's examples use US and European cities, but the geometry does not stop at their borders.
Can I measure between a city and a non-city place?
Yes, by setting the other point by search or coordinates — or switch to Distance Between Two Places, which is built for arbitrary points.
Why is my result different from a flight time estimate?
Flight times include routing, winds and procedures on top of the surface distance this page measures. The distance is the stable ingredient; the time is the variable one.
Does it show driving distance too?
No — this page is the straight-line instrument. The driving figure lives in the Driving Distance Calculator, and comparing the two is often the insight.
How do I share a pair I measured?
The measured pair is encoded in the page, so the link you copy reopens the same two cities for whoever receives it.
